title: Twilio
content:
## Overview

Twilio is a cloud communications platform that enables your Emergent app to send SMS messages, make voice calls, and deliver notifications. This integration is ideal for apps that need to verify users via SMS, send transactional alerts, or implement two-factor authentication.

<Note>
Twilio charges per message or call. Review [Twilio's pricing](https://www.twilio.com/pricing) before implementing SMS or voice features at scale.
</Note>

## Prerequisites

Before integrating Twilio, you'll need:

- A Twilio account ([sign up here](https://www.twilio.com/try-twilio))
- A Twilio phone number (purchased from your Twilio console)
- Your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token (found in your Twilio console dashboard)

## Setting up Twilio in Emergent

<Steps>
<Step title="Obtain your Twilio credentials">
Log in to your [Twilio Console](https://console.twilio.com) and locate your **Account SID** and **Auth Token** on the dashboard. Keep these values handy — you'll need them in the next step.

If you haven't already, purchase a phone number from **Phone Numbers → Buy a Number** in the Twilio console. This number will be the sender for your SMS messages.
</Step>

<Step title="Add credentials to your Emergent app">
In your Emergent chat, tell the AI agents to add Twilio environment variables:

```
Add these environment variables:
- TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID: <your Account SID>
- TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN: <your Auth Token>
- TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER: <your purchased phone number in E.164 format>
```

The agents will securely store these in your app's environment configuration.
</Step>

<Step title="Describe your SMS or voice feature">
Tell Emergent what you want to build. For example:

- _"Add SMS verification when users sign up — send a 6-digit code to their phone number."_
- _"Send an SMS notification when an order ships, including the tracking number."_
- _"Let users opt in to receive weekly SMS reminders about their appointments."_

The AI agents will scaffold the necessary API calls using the Twilio Node.js or Python SDK (depending on your app's stack).
</Step>

<Step title="Test your integration">
Once the agents deploy your changes, test the SMS or voice functionality in your app. Check your Twilio console's **Logs → Messaging** or **Logs → Calls** to confirm messages are being sent and to debug any delivery issues.
</Step>
</Steps>

## Common use cases

<CardGroup cols={2}>
<Card title="Phone verification" icon="shield-check">
Send a one-time passcode via SMS during signup or login to verify a user's phone number.
</Card>

<Card title="Transactional alerts" icon="bell">
Notify users of important events—order confirmations, password resets, appointment reminders.
</Card>

<Card title="Two-factor authentication" icon="lock">
Enhance security by requiring an SMS code in addition to a password when users log in.
</Card>

<Card title="Marketing campaigns" icon="megaphone">
Send promotional messages to opted-in users. Ensure compliance with local regulations (e.g., TCPA, GDPR).
</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Example implementation

Below is an example of how Emergent agents might implement an SMS verification flow using Twilio's Node.js SDK:

<CodeGroup>
```javascript Node.js
import twilio from 'twilio';

const client = twilio(
  process.env.TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID,
  process.env.TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
);

export async function sendVerificationCode(phoneNumber, code) {
  await client.messages.create({
    body: `Your verification code is: ${code}`,
    from: process.env.TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER,
    to: phoneNumber
  });
}
```

```python Python
from twilio.rest import Client
import os

client = Client(
    os.environ['TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID'],
    os.environ['TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN']
)

def send_verification_code(phone_number: str, code: str):
    client.messages.create(
        body=f'Your verification code is: {code}',
        from_=os.environ['TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER'],
        to=phone_number
    )
```
</CodeGroup>

<Info>
Phone numbers must be in E.164 format (e.g., `+14155552671`). Emergent agents typically validate and format numbers automatically when you describe your feature requirements.
</Info>

## Testing and debugging

<Accordion title="Messages aren't being delivered">
- Verify your phone number is in E.164 format with a country code (e.g., `+1` for US).
- Check Twilio's console under **Logs → Messaging** for error codes.
- Ensure your Twilio account is not in trial mode or has sufficient credit balance.
- Confirm the recipient's carrier isn't blocking messages (some carriers filter shortcodes or toll-free numbers).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Environment variables not loading">
If your app can't read `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` or other variables, ask the agents:

_"Verify my Twilio environment variables are set correctly."_

The agents will check your configuration and redeploy if needed.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Rate limiting or throttling errors">
Twilio enforces rate limits on message sending. If you're sending high volumes, consider:

- Queueing messages with a background job processor.
- Requesting a rate limit increase from Twilio support.
- Using Twilio's Messaging Services for better throughput.
</Accordion>

## Best practices

- **Validate phone numbers** before sending to avoid wasted credits on invalid destinations.
- **Respect opt-outs**: Honor unsubscribe requests immediately and maintain a suppression list.
- **Use short, clear messages**: SMS has a 160-character limit (longer messages are split and billed per segment).
- **Monitor delivery status**: Use Twilio webhooks to track delivery, failures, and user replies.
- **Secure your credentials**: Never commit `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` to version control. Emergent stores environment variables securely for you.

## Compliance and regulations

<Warning>
SMS marketing is subject to legal restrictions in many countries. In the US, you must obtain explicit consent before sending promotional messages (TCPA). In the EU, GDPR requires clear consent and easy opt-out mechanisms.

Always consult legal counsel if you're sending marketing or promotional messages.
</Warning>

## Next steps

- Explore Twilio's [Verify API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify/api) for built-in OTP workflows.
- Add WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger support via Twilio's Programmable Messaging.
- Integrate Twilio Voice to build interactive voice response (IVR) systems or place outbound calls.

<Tip>
You can extend your Twilio integration by describing additional features in chat. For example: _"Add a webhook to log SMS replies in our database"_ or _"Send an email fallback if SMS delivery fails."_
</Tip>
